cards.back: Unsupervised partitioning of unlabelled data so that **intra-cluster distance is minimized** (tight clusters) and **inter-cluster distance is maximized** (well-separated).
Hierarchical, Partitional (K-means), Density-based (DBSCAN), Grid-based, Model-based (GMM), Fuzzy. Splits: hierarchical vs partitional; hard vs soft.
Agglomerative = bottom-up (start singletons, merge closest). Divisive = top-down (start one cluster, split). Both irreversible. Output = dendrogram (no pre-set k).
Single link = MIN (closest pair); Complete link = MAX (farthest pair); Group average = mean of all pairs; Centroid = centroid distance; Ward = min increase in squared error.
Tree whose merge heights = dissimilarity of merged clusters. Cut horizontally at a height → a flat clustering. Hierarchical needs no pre-set number of clusters.
Pick K + random centroids → (1) Assign each point to nearest centroid → (2) Update centroid = mean of its points → repeat to convergence. Complexity O(nKId).
Random init → varies run to run, local optimum; must pick K; sensitive to outliers; assumes spherical equal-size clusters. Centroid = mean; closeness = Euclidean.
$SSE=\sum_k\sum_{x\in C_k}\text{dist}(m_k,x)^2$. SSE always falls as K rises → can't minimize it for K; instead plot SSE vs K and pick the **elbow**.
Start with one cluster; repeatedly split the **highest-SSE** cluster using K-means (K=2) until #clusters=K. Hybrid of divisive hierarchical + K-means; less init-sensitive.
Fails on differing sizes, differing densities, non-globular shapes. Outliers pull centroids & inflate SSE → remove before clustering. Text → use cosine similarity.
K-means = **hard-assignment EM** for a Gaussian mixture with equal spherical covariances & weights. Assignment ≈ E-step, update ≈ M-step; minimizes within-cluster variation (=SSE).
As dimensions grow, data becomes sparse; distance/density lose meaning (classification & clustering degrade). Motivates dimensionality reduction (PCA, SVD).
Principal components: rank-ordered by **variance**, mutually **orthogonal/uncorrelated**, **linear combinations** of features. PC1 = direction of max variance; PC2 = max variance ⟂ PC1.

1) Mean-center (standardize). 2) Covariance matrix. 3) Eigenvectors (=PCs) & eigenvalues (=variance). 4) Order by descending eigenvalue. 5) Project onto top-k eigenvectors: $z=\text{eigvec}^T(x-\mu)$.
Data → μ=(4.5,5); covariance $\begin{bmatrix}2.92&3.67\\3.67&5.67\end{bmatrix}$; eigenvalues λ=8.22, 0.38; PC1 eigenvector X₁=0.69X₂ ≈ (0.57,0.82).
$A=U\Sigma V^T$: U=left singular vectors (m×m), Σ=singular values (m×n), Vᵀ=right singular vectors (n×n). U,V orthogonal; works for non-square A. σᵢ=√λᵢ of AᵀA; V=eigenvectors of AᵀA; uᵢ=(1/σᵢ)Avᵢ.
PCA = SVD of the **centered** data matrix. PCs = right singular vectors V; eigenvalues of covariance = $\lambda_i = \sigma_i^2$. Both = linear dimensionality reduction for continuous data.

ML uses hand-crafted features for specific tasks. DL learns a **hierarchy of features automatically** across many hidden layers (representation learning). DL needs more data + compute; scales with data.
Dense on 224×224×3 = 150,528 inputs → >1M weights in layer 1. CNN is **sparse** (local patches) with **weight sharing** → far fewer params, spatially aware.
Output size $O=\frac{n-f+2p}{s}+1$. Params per conv layer $=f\cdot f\cdot c\cdot k$ (k filters, c channels). Valid=no pad (shrinks); Same=preserve size.
Input → Conv(+ReLU) → Pool → FC → Softmax → Output. Pooling down-samples (max or average), **no learnable params**. Filter channels must = input channels.
Input 227×227×3; Conv1 11×11, stride 4, 96 filters → (227−11)/4+1 = 55 → **55×55×96**. Deeper: H,W shrink while depth grows. Params(Conv1)=11·11·3·96.
Each step t: agent takes action Aₜ, observes Oₜ, gets reward Rₜ; environment returns Oₜ₊₁, Rₜ₊₁. Goal = maximize cumulative reward via trial-and-error.
Markov state: future independent of past given present (sufficient statistic). Fully-observable RL = MDP ⟨S,A,P,R,γ⟩. Partially observable = POMDP (infer hidden state).
$G_t=\sum_k\gamma^k R_{t+k+1}$. $V^\pi(s)=E_\pi[G_t|s]$; $Q^\pi(s,a)=E_\pi[G_t|s,a]$. Bellman: $V^\pi(s)=E[R+\gamma V(S')]$. $\pi^*(s)=\arg\max_a Q^*(s,a)$.
$Q(s,a)\leftarrow Q(s,a)+\alpha[r+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s',a')-Q(s,a)]$. Model-free, off-policy; bracket = TD error. Deep Q-Learning approximates Q with a neural net.
Exploitation = use best-known action (max immediate reward, safe). Exploration = try new actions (gather info, risky). Must trade off (e.g. ε-greedy).
$\text{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\text{softmax}(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}})V$. Q=XWQ, K=XWK, V=XWV. Scores = Q·Kᵀ scaled by √dₖ, softmaxed, weighting V.

PE injects word **order** (Transformers are parallel, no recurrence): $PE_{(k,2i)}=\sin(k/n^{2i/d})$, cos for odd, added to embeddings. Multi-head = parallel attentions on different relationships. Decoder uses a **look-ahead mask** (−∞ on future) for autoregression.
GPT = decoder-only Transformer, next-token prediction. GPT-1 pretraining; GPT-2 zero/few-shot; GPT-3 few-shot at scale (175B); GPT-3.5 instruction-tuning + **RLHF** (ChatGPT); GPT-4 **multimodal**.

**Prompting** = craft input, no training (zero/few-shot, CoT). **RAG** = retrieve external docs → add to input (beats knowledge cutoff), no weight change. **Fine-tuning** = update weights on curated data (LoRA/QLoRA).
Large LM (GPT-4): billions–trillions params, massive data, generic, high-end GPUs, costly. Small LM (Vicuna-1B): millions–hundreds of millions, small corpus, specific tasks, consumer hardware, cheap.
